artworks.title: The Daughters of Cecrops Finding the Child Erichthonius
artworks.description: Jordaens' Antwerp canvas shows Cecrops' three daughters opening Athena's forbidden basket — Aglauros among the sisters who glimpse the serpent-child Erichthonius and seal their doom.

artworks.title: Daughters of Cecrops Discovering Erichthonius
artworks.description: Rubens' Courtauld oil sketch returns to the same Athenian crisis: the Cecropids uncover Erichthonius — Aglauros' curiosity as the prelude to envy, Mercury, and the stone that Ovid makes of her.

artworks.title: Athena Pursuing Aglauros (Attic red-figure kylix)
artworks.description: On this Attic cup the goddess herself pursues Aglauros — a rare vase naming the middle daughter of Cecrops in the aftermath of the opened basket, when Athena's anger still runs through Athens.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Mercury's gold, Minerva's Envy, and Aglauros turned to stone — Ovid's Athenian sister who bars the god from Herse.

popCulture.title: Aglaurus, daughter of Cecrops
popCulture.description: Cecrops' middle daughter — jealous gatekeeper of her sister's beauty and the princess who becomes rock.

popCulture.title: Herse
popCulture.description: The sister Mercury loved — Herse's beauty is the bait that makes Aglauros' envy fatal.
